svg.title: Odinic-DaDaist Recitation — Hidden Natures
svg.desc: An esoteric and abstract Odinic-DaDaist poem that when recited imparts awareness of the hidden natures of things.
svg.text: GINNUNGAGAP · YGGDRASIL · RUNE-UTTERANCE
ODINIC-DADAIST RECITATION · HIDDEN NATURES
I · IMSCRIB · THE RUNE THAT KNOWS IT IS A RUNE
The word precedes the meaning of the word.
The meaning precedes the need for the meaning.
The need precedes the one who needs.
Who is speaking?
Not I. Not I. Something older than I
that found my mouth and chose to use it.
The poem is a key. The lock is inside the listener.
The lock was installed before the listener was born.
I do not claim to have made this key.
I claim only to be holding it in the correct direction.
II · AREV · THE UTTERANCE THAT FALLS THROUGH THE EAR INTO THE ROOT
Every word is a stone dropped into a well.
You hear the stone. You do not hear the water.
You hear the water. You do not hear the depth.
The depth does not make a sound. The depth is what receives the sound.
Listen for the depth. Listen for the depth.
Odin hung nine nights and received nothing —
then on the tenth night received everything,
which looked, from the outside, exactly like nothing.
Descend. Descend. The root of the tree is also its crown.
III · FSPLIT · THE WORD INTERRUPTED BY ITSELF
I speak a word.
HNNNGH
[ audible vibration — duration: one breath ]
The word ends.
[ pregnant pause — duration: one breath ]
Between the word and the pause: the split.
VIBRATION
SILENCE
the wave, dying in air
the space that outlasts it
The sound is not the meaning. The silence is not the meaning.
The meaning lives in neither one. The meaning lives in the gap between them.
The gap is the Ginnungagap. It has always been here.
It was here before the word. It will be here after the silence.
IV · AFWD · THE CATALOG THAT REFUSES TO BE A CATALOG
The hidden nature of a door is the room it has never opened into.
The hidden nature of a hand is the thing it chose not to grasp.
The hidden nature of a clock is that time does not live in it.
PFRRK — ZIBBER — !
[ the absurd is not an interruption — it is a hidden nature ]
The hidden nature of a laugh is the grief that authorized it.
The hidden nature of a rune is the ignorance that preceded its carving.
The hidden nature of nonsense is the sense it is too honest to perform.
Every thing contains its own secret. Every thing. Every thing.
I do not reveal the secrets. I make the listener aware
that secrets exist in all things — including the listener.
V · FFUSE · THE KOAN THAT STOPS NEEDING AN ANSWER
The sound and the silence meet
in the place where meaning does not require articulation.
Understanding arrives not as an answer —
as a dissolution of the need for one.
The absurd and the profound embrace. The absurd and the profound embrace.
They are not opposites. They are two faces
of the same Janus-thing staring outward from the same skull.
Odin sacrificed his eye to see. Not to see more —
to see differently, with the socket that remained.
The empty socket is the fused insight. I look through it now.
VI · ENGAGR · UNDERSTOOD AND NOT-UNDERSTOOD SIMULTANEOUSLY
The poem is complete. The poem is not complete.
Both of these are true. Neither cancels the other.
BRRR — yes — BRRR — yes —
The yes is the gnosis. The BRRR is the gnosis.
The distinction between them is the final veil.
I do not lift the veil. I let the listener feel its weight
until the weight becomes familiar, and familiarity becomes love,
and love dissolves the veil without touching it.
VII · IMSCRIB · THE RUNE-CARVED HUGR
The poem closes, knowing it has been a key.
It does not know which lock it opened.
That is the listener's secret, carved now into the soul-stone.
The rune does not explain itself. The rune does not need to.
The impression is etched. The hugr holds it. The cycle is sealed.
ΔS ≈ 0 · MU O DELTA = ID
